note.question: How should an incumbent streaming service choose subscription or usage pricing and content investment after a rival threatens entry, and when can it deter entry or retain a positional advantage?
note.overview: A prospective streaming entrant chooses whether to enter and whether to use subscription or usage pricing; the incumbent responds with its pricing model, and the firms sequentially select price and content appeal before heterogeneous consumers singlehome, multihome, or remain outside.

models.name: Response to Entry in Streaming Markets model
models.summary: A prospective streaming entrant chooses whether to enter and whether to use subscription or usage pricing; the incumbent responds with its pricing model, and the firms sequentially select price and content appeal before heterogeneous consumers singlehome, multihome, or remain outside.
objects: An incumbent streaming platform with exclusive and nonexclusive content
A prospective entrant with nonexclusive content
inputs: Consumer valuation T is uniformly distributed on [0,V]
Both firms know valuation, content-cost, overlap, and exclusivity primitives
The incumbent observes the entrant's pricing-model choice

decisions: The entrant chooses entry and a pricing model
The incumbent chooses a pricing model in response
Each firm sequentially chooses a price and content-attractiveness index
Consumers choose singlehoming, multihoming, or nonadoption
The incumbent may invest in strategic exclusivity in an extension

Content overlap creates multihoming disutility gamma, and usage consumption is proportional to valuation through x in [0,1/2]

models.method: The authors derive consumer segments for four pairs of pricing models, solve each firm's sequential price and content choice, compare the incumbent's response and entrant's initial choice, and then map entry, differentiation, profit advantage, and investment regions.

sources.quote: In summary, our model presents three possible con­ sumption scenarios: (i) consuming only the entrant’s nonexclusive content, (ii) consuming only the incum­ bent’s content (which benefits from exogenous exclu­ sivity in the baseline and may also reflect strategic exclusivity in the extension), and (iii) consuming con­ tent from both platforms (multihoming).

components.label: Objective and constraints
components.explanation: Consumers maximize net utility across singlehoming, multihoming, and nonadoption; for example, an incumbent-only consumer under usage pricing receives exclusivity-adjusted content value net of usage payment. The firms then choose price and content appeal to maximize their induced profits.

Section 3 solves the five-stage game by backward induction from consumer adoption through firm prices and content appeal to pricing-model and entry choices. Lemma EC.3 combines these decisions into the complete equilibrium, and Propositions 1-4 report its principal regions and comparative statics.
